visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with glasses and a black polo shirt stands against a background of animated fireworks at night. An overlay image of three monochromatic faces appears in the center, partially obscured by horizontal static lines. He gestures with his right hand holding an orange pen. (2) The scene shifts to show MRI brain scans. A chart labeled with '5-year group', '15-year group', and '25-year group' displays cross-sections of the brain with various colorful highlights (green, red, yellow). The man continues to speak in a small inset. (3) A digital interface titled 'AI-based Brain Assessment System' is shown. It features a 3D grayscale rendering of a human brain alongside analysis metrics and buttons like 'Analyze'. The man points at the screen. (4) The camera returns to the man against the fireworks background. He uses expansive hand movements and holds an orange stylus. He finishes by looking around with a confused expression, touching his head and gesturing toward the space around him.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A male voice speaks with high clarity and a quick pace, delivering a monologue in Mandarin. The voice is energetic and authoritative. An upbeat, electronic background track with a steady kick drum and synth pads plays at a lower volume, providing a driving rhythm. (2) A sharp 'whoosh' sound effect punctuates a transition. The speaker introduces technical terms like 'BrainProbe' and 'MRI' with precise articulation. The music maintains a constant 124 BPM. (3) The speaker's tone becomes narrative as he explains 'hacker attacks' in the brain. A digital 'ding' or UI click sound is heard when pointing out data points on the imaginary screen. (4) The BGM continues uninterrupted. The speaker's vocal arousal increases slightly as he discusses the value of de-stigmatization. The recording is studio-clean with no environmental noise. (5) In the final phase, the speaker adopts a more casual, slightly questioning tone, lowering the intensity slightly. The music track ends with a clean cut as the speaker makes a joke about 'not being real'.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: List-based: Hook -> Problem (Stigma/Slow Diagnosis) -> Innovation (AI-BrainProbe) -> Mechanism (Hacker analogy) -> Proof (Data) -> Social Value -> Outro
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a science communication piece to announce a breakthrough in medical AI technology from Taiwan. It explains how the 'BrainProbe' system uses MRI and AI to diagnose schizophrenia with high accuracy and track physical brain changes like a 'hacker attack,' aiming to provide objective medical evidence to reduce societal stigma and help patients understand their condition.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The video uses a high-arousal delivery style common in social media 'explainer' videos, combining professional medical data with an approachable analogy to ensure high engagement and information retention.
